messages:
alice: incident-bot just paged me for INC-2026-03 — spike of 500s from /v1/generate in us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T12:14:10Z. p95 latency up from 180ms -> 2.3s. frontend error rate jumped to 6.8%. tagging @ben and @carla to triage.

incident-bot: PAGED oncall: alice (primary). Severity: S2. Customer-impacting: yes (some hosts 5xx). Link: https://observability/redwood/incidents/INC-2026-03

ben: ack, looking. grabbing logs and query patterns now. which model pool is this hitting?

alice: looks like requests are hitting rwd-model-prod-gpu-a (quantized gpt-small variant). traffic split unchanged. no deploy in last 30m per deploy-bot.

carla: I see a CPU-side backpressure OOM trace on the model-worker logs around 12:14:12Z, plus a flurry of session token errors from the auth layer. attaching snippets below.

carla: ```
[12:14:11Z] gpu-worker-7 ERROR kv_cache: failed to allocate 64MB chunk: OOM
[12:14:12Z] gpu-worker-7 INFO session: invalid-token from 10.2.5.43
[12:14:13Z] router-3 WARN reroute: route delay 120ms
```

dinesh: I ran a quick metric query: active sessions spiked by ~40% at 12:13:50Z from a single upstream client IP range (54.203.*).* Could be a client-side retry storm.

alice: customer-impact list: a few enterprise tenants reported generation timeouts, internal dashboard shows ~12 requests/min failing for top-10 customers in us-west-2. priority: surface mitigation and decide on revert/rollback if config change.

eva: FYI no config deploys, but we did flip a routing policy at 12:10Z to route low-latency tier to gpu-a to reduce cost (PR #1248). maybe related.

ben: hypothesis 1: routing change concentrated more concurrent long-sequence requests onto gpu-a and exhausted KV cache memory leading to OOMs and 5xx.

ben: hypothesis 2: a noisy client generating massive short retries caused auth token thrash, exhausting session table and causing downstream errors.

carla: I'm collecting full worker logs and will attach a tarball to the incident doc. also capturing heap and GPU usage graphs for the last 30m.

alice: short-term mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily shift a portion of traffic back to gpu-b pool (route weight change), 2) throttle upstream client CIDR at edge, 3) bump KV cache eviction threshold on gpu-a. Which one can we run quickly?

ben: I can do a route weight change now — do a controlled 20% shift off gpu-a to gpu-b, monitor for 5m. who owns routing change? @dinesh?

dinesh: I own the routing policy. I'll do 20% shift in 2 minutes and watch SLOs. prepping rollback plan to put weight back if things worsen.

incident-bot: ACTION created: routing-shift (owner: dinesh).

carla: attaching quick flamegraph of kv cache pressure before/after spike. looks like large sequences causing many cache entries and then thrash. might need a model-level prefix caching cap.

alice: timeline so far: 12:10Z routing policy flip -> 12:13:50Z spike in requests from single CIDR -> 12:14:11Z OOMs & 5xx surge -> 12:17Z paged. we need to confirm causality.

ben: dinesh, please post confirmation when shift done. I'll watch error rate and p95. if error rate drops within 3m of shift, that supports hypothesis 1.

dinesh: route-weight change pushed at 12:21:00Z: gpu-a 60% -> 40%, gpu-b increased accordingly. monitoring.

ben: p95 dropped to 860ms after ~90s, error rate down to 2.1% at 12:23:00Z. still above baseline but improving.

alice: good. mark experiment: controlled routing shift. outcome: partial remediation. owner: dinesh.

carla: still seeing token errors from that CIDR. can we rate-limit that client at the edge? could prevent session table blowout.

dinesh: I can add an ACL throttle for 54.203.0.0/16 to 10rps at 12:27Z. applying now.

incident-bot: ACTION updated: add-acl-throttle (owner: dinesh).

ben: after throttle, token errors dropped sharply and session table usage returned to normal by 12:29Z. p95 stabilized ~220ms by 12:30Z. looks like combined mitigation fixed it.

alice: can we capture root cause hypothesis list for the RCA: A) routing policy concentrated long sequences onto gpu-a exposing an existing kv-cache capacity bug; B) a noisy client amplified the failure by retrying tokens and filling session table. We should plan a revert test for the routing policy to validate (put original policy back during a low-traffic window) and a scoped mitigation to harden kv-cache on gpu-a.

carla: agree. I propose experiments: 1) replay small sample of sequences against gpu-a in staging with load-tuned kv-cache to reproduce OOM; 2) add guardrail to eviction logic to refuse huge prefix growth; 3) add alert for session-table near-capacity. owners: carla (runtime), ben (observability), dinesh (network/routing).

alice: action items captured in incident doc. we should schedule a short post-incident sync at 16:00Z today. I'll hand the oncall to ben at 13:00Z — leaving notes for next oncall. :white_check_mark:

ben: taking over oncall at 13:00Z. will follow up on experiments and coordinate with runtime team.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. pinned summary: routing change + noisy client => partial outage, mitigations: route shift + ACL throttle, next steps: kv-cache guardrails + replay tests.

alice: thanks team. posting links: logs tarball https://s3.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-03/logs.tgz, graphs https://observability/redwood/graphs/INC-2026-03.

ben: I'll add a short appendix to the incident doc with queries, commands used, and the exact route change diff for reproducibility.

carla: uploading heap dumps and the flamegraph now.

dinesh: will schedule the revert test window for 03/16 02:00-03:00 UTC (low traffic) and coordinate with runtime to watch memory metrics.

alice: closing live thread for now — moving to RCA channel: please continue updates in #postmortems/INC-2026-03 and add owners to the action items.

incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (handed off to postmortems).
